To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IHF bends DNA to stimulate transcription of the phage lambda PL promoter.
IHF stimulates the PL promoter by bending the DNA to bring in close proximity the UP sequence to the promoter core elements and by participating in protein–protein contacts with the αCTDs.
the stimulation of transcription by IHFs requires an intact α‐CTD and affects initial binding of RNA Pol to the promoter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of transcriptional stimulation of a bacterial promoter by IHF and the role of a distal UP element in this stimulation.
the role of IHF in the activation of the PL promoter.
the participation of a distant UP element, IHF and the αCTD in transcription initiation from the PL promoter of phage λ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IHF stimulates PL transcription by binding to DNA, bending the DNA and participating in protein–protein contacts with the αCTDs of the RNA polymerase.
the IHF‐binding site and the αCTD participate in the stimulation of PL transcription.
the stimulation of the PL promoter by IHF is a consequence of a combination of DNA bending and direct protein–protein interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IHF is a dual‐acting factor, stimulating the PL promoter by bending the DNA and by protein–protein interactions.
the UP element is a target for IHF binding, and that IHF bends the PL DNA to bring the UP element closer to the promoter to facilitate the interaction with the αCTC of RNA polymerase.

both the UP and the IHF binding sites are important for the stimulation of the PL promoter, and that both the αCTD and IHF participate in protein–DNA and protein–protein interactions to achieve this stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stimulation of the PL promoter by IHF is a two‐pronged process involving the bending of DNA to bring the UP element closer to the core promoter and the participation of the αCTDs in protein–protein contacts.
the PL promoter can be stimulated by IHF in two distinct ways.
the PL promoter is regulated by a distant UP element and IHF.
